memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They received from Moses all the offerings the Israelites had brought to carry out the work of constructing the sanctuary. And the people continued to bring freewill offerings morning after morning." - Exod 36:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Morning after morning." That short phrase carries the weight of this verse.

The first day of giving is easy. Enthusiasm is high, everyone is watching, the moment feels significant. It is the fifth morning, the tenth morning, the morning when nobody notices, that reveals what is actually in the heart.

Israel kept coming. Day after day, people walked out with something in their hands.

Most of the Christian life is built exactly here — not in dramatic decisions but in repeated ones. Prayer morning after morning. Kindness in the same marriage morning after morning. Faithfulness at the same job, with the same difficult colleague, morning after morning.

Paul knew we would tire of this: let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up (Gal 6:9). Jesus spoke of taking up the cross daily (Luke 9:23) — not once, daily.

There is nothing glamorous about the tenth morning. But that is where character is formed and where God's work actually gets built.

What did you do yesterday that you should do again today?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tempted to give up because the initial enthusiasm has faded?
2. What daily faithfulness is God asking of you right now?
3. Is your walk with God built on moments or on habits?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me faithful in the ordinary mornings when no one is watching. Let me not grow weary. Amen.
